scope.flow: ETWAP-anchored mint and redeem caps in early/new markets
scope.environment: protocol market with bootstrap no-cap phase and exponential TWAP of base supply
evidence: The protocol throttles growth and exits using a time weighted average of base supply (ETWAP). Two cap rules are relevant:

ETWAP is updated inside _calculateMarketState using an exponential half life. In the same block, elapsedTime = 0, so lastETWAPBaseSupply does not move. In the first block of market activity, ETWAP is effectively zero. The mint and redeem caps both anchor to this stale value.
Phase 1 (bootstrap no-cap): Attacker performs a very large first mint while base supply is below 2^noCapLimit. Bootstrap rules apply, so the mint is effectively uncapped.

Phase 2 (same block redeem): Attacker immediately redeems roughly 99 percent in the same block. ETWAP is still near zero, so the redeem cap is loose. The attacker drains down to a small S_cur, but keeps it above the bootstrap threshold so the system considers the market out of bootstrap.

Phase 3 (DoS window): Now that bootstrap is off, the mint cap applies. With ETWAP tiny, the inequality S_post ≤ 2·ETWAP blocks any honest mint. The window can last many minutes because ETWAP climbs with an exponential half life, and the attacker can keep it low relative to S_cur by touching the market periodically to advance lastUpdateTimestamp while keeping ETWAP lagging.

entities.name: bootstrap no-cap threshold (2^noCapLimit)
evidence: Phase 1 (bootstrap no-cap): Attacker performs a very large first mint while base supply is below 2^noCapLimit. Bootstrap rules apply, so the mint is effectively uncapped.

Phase 2 (same block redeem): Attacker immediately redeems roughly 99 percent in the same block. ETWAP is still near zero, so the redeem cap is loose. The attacker drains down to a small S_cur, but keeps it above the bootstrap threshold so the system considers the market out of bootstrap.

Bootstrap boundary: noCapLimit allows a large first mint with no cap. The next action in the same block can redeem most of it while ETWAP is still zero, then leave S_cur just above 2^noCapLimit, which flips on the strict mint cap for everyone else.

statements.text: _calculateMarketState updates lastETWAPBaseSupply only when elapsedTime > 0, so in the same block ETWAP stays at its stale near-zero value and both caps anchor to it.
evidence: ETWAP is updated inside _calculateMarketState using an exponential half life. In the same block, elapsedTime = 0, so lastETWAPBaseSupply does not move. In the first block of market activity, ETWAP is effectively zero. The mint and redeem caps both anchor to this stale value.
Root cause: _calculateMarketState updates lastETWAPBaseSupply only when elapsedTime > 0, and the update uses an exponential half life (see DebtMath).
Asymmetry: Mint cap is strict with small ETWAP. Redeem cap is permissive with small ETWAP.

statements.text: When the mint cap applies, a mint should be permitted only if the post-mint base supply satisfies S_post ≤ 2·ETWAP, so a tiny ETWAP should not by itself block all positive mints.
evidence: Let S_cur be current base supply and ETWAP the exponential TWAP of base supply. The cap enforces
When ETWAP is very small, any positive mint fails.
Mint cap: S_post ≤ max(2·ETWAP, S_cur + β·S_cur) with small β, or add a minimum absolute mint allowance to avoid total DoS when ETWAP is tiny.

statements.text: The redeem cap should require a post-state floor tied to ETWAP so that a tiny ETWAP does not permit very large redemptions.
evidence: Requires a post state floor tied to ETWAP, for examplen When ETWAP is very small, very large redemptions pass.
Redeem cap: S_post ≥ max(α·ETWAP, γ·S_cur) with γ in the 50 to 70 percent range. This prevents near total drains when ETWAP is tiny.

statements.text: On the first non-zero supply update, ETWAP should be seeded to base supply (or a large fraction) rather than remaining at a near-zero anchor.
evidence: Seed ETWAP on first growth: On the first non zero supply update, initialize lastETWAPBaseSupply = baseSupply (or a large fraction like 80 percent). This removes the near zero anchor.

statements.text: Honest new lenders should be able to mint (market liveness for growth) rather than having all honest deposits blocked.
evidence: No direct theft occurs, but honest growth is blocked and exits remain relatively unconstrained during the lag. In young or rapidly expanding markets, this breaks liveness for new lenders and can be used to shape liquidity around the attacker’s schedule.
Mint DoS for a sustained period after the attacker executes the yo-yo sequence. Honest deposits revert with E_LEX_MintCapExceeded.

ambiguities: Report does not state whether the attacker is permissionless/unauthorized; no explicit anyone-can-call statement.
Whether the periodic touch in Phase 3 is required or optional for the DoS window is not fully specified.
Exact numeric values of ETWAP, S_cur, and noCapLimit are not given.
Whether the same-block redeem of ~99 percent is bounded by any other check is not stated.
